questions.prompt: What must be true for a TypeScript import to work in an application?
options: The source module specifier, compiler resolution, package exports and actual runtime/bundler must agree.
The compiler always rewrites every alias into a working runtime path.
Any filename extension works with every runtime.
Type-only imports create runtime values automatically.
questions.answer_key: The source module specifier, compiler resolution, package exports and actual runtime/bundler must agree.
questions.explanation: Type checking and runtime module loading are related but distinct responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Dynamic Imports”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with import() and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with import() and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “import()”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Dynamic Imports”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check asynchronous module loading, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume integration with code splitting is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check asynchronous module loading, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Asynchronous module loading”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
